resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc (tab t.0, no images) that covers the full EOLR case set for Roux LSE. Every case has a 2-gen M/U alg plus a written way to understand it. It is split into 9 sections, one per EO case. Each section header gives a short code for the case and the bad-edge positions in the reference orientation: 3/1 'arrow', 4/0, 2o/2, 2a/2, 1/1, 2o/0, 2a/0, 0/2 and 4/2 (6-flip). The solved-EO case is not covered. Inside each section, cases are named by where the two L/R edges (the UL/UR pieces) are relative to the bad edges: Stacked, Good, Bottom, Adjacent, Bad, Opposite, Best, Great, Decent, Mixed Adjacent, Oriented/Misoriented Opposite, UF Adjacent/Separated/Opposite, Sides and so on. Each name heading lists every L/R placement it covers and then gives one alg. Every case then has a one-line 'Recognition:' rule and either a 'Solution:' (the intuitive breakdown, ending with oriented centres) or an 'MC Solution:' (ending with misoriented centres, finished by an M), and sometimes both. Most breakdowns reduce the case to a simpler named case ('... Good 3/1 from there'), and those references are clickable links to the target heading. Together they form a chain that leads back to a few 3/1 arrow base cases. I counted 51 named cases covering 94 listed L/R placements: 3/1 has 5 (14 placements), 4/0 4 (6), 2o/2 6 (8), 2a/2 7 (14), 1/1 9 (15), 2o/0 6 (9), 2a/0 7 (15), 0/2 4 (8) and 4/2 3 (5). Linked from rouxcubing.com (LSE > EOLR), resources.rouxers.com (Last Six Edges > EOLR Docs), the Roux Reader LSE chapter and rouxl.es. Saved: plain-text and HTML exports. Structure: EO group (bad-edge pattern code + positions) > named L/R-placement class (with list of placements) > alg > Recognition > Solution / MC Solution, with internal links to the case each breakdown reduces to.

resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc. It is a compact, full two-handed ('2H') EOLR alg list tuned for M moves done with the right hand. The top has 4 numbered footnotes that set AUF conditions for some cases: AUF so the R, L or F face corners match the DF edge, and (RH version only) which of two solutions to use depending on whether the UL/UR stickers match the L/R corners. There are 11 sections, each headed by its bad-edge pattern code and an EO diagram: 11 embedded 3D cube images, all yellow with misoriented edge stickers in purple. The sections are 3/1F and 3/1B (arrow pointing front or back), 4/0, 0/2, 2o/0, 2o/2, 2a/0, 2a/2 (whose header still contains a stray 'THING.jpg' filename), 1/1F, 1/1B and 6-flip. Each line is one case, keyed by the two L/R edge positions (e.g. an 'XX YY:' pair), followed by an M/U alg. A few lines also have a footnote digit, a second alternative ('or'), or a parenthesised alg whose meaning is not explained. Count: 123 cases. 3/1F 15, 3/1B 15, 4/0 5, 0/2 5, 2o/0 9, 2o/2 9, 2a/0 15, 2a/2 15, 1/1F 15, 1/1B 15, 6-flip 5. 7 lines give two options and 5 are parenthesised. Almost every alg is M/U 2-gen; one 2o/0 case uses R/r moves. Footer: 'Last updated: 3/4/20'. There is no recognition text or explanation. Saved: text and HTML exports and the 11 EO diagrams (tdm-rh-imgs/). Structure: Footnote legend (AUF conditions) > EO-pattern section with EO diagram > one line per L/R position pair with alg (occasional 'or' alternative, parenthesised alg, footnote digit).

resources.level: advanced (EOLRb, i.e. EOLR that also sets up 4b/ULUR by looking at corner colours)
resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc. It is an unpolished personal working document that mixes EOLR algs with EOLRb solutions. EOLRb choices use the corner colours so that the UL/UR edges finish already solved relative to the corners. A notation line says cases marked with a star are EOLRb solutions. Part 1 is a case list in 10 sections: Arrow (F), 6-Flip, 4/0, 2o/2 (LR), 2o/0 (FB), 0/2, 2a/0 (BL), 2a/2 (BL), 1/1 (F), 1/1 (B). Each has the same EO diagrams as TDM's sheet, 10 images in total. There are about 67 entries keyed by L/R edge position pair or by a U/D placement pattern. Many entries branch on a corner-relation condition: whether the L/R edge sits under SAME, OPP (opposite) or ADJ (adjacent) coloured corners. There are 32 stars, some entries are in red text, and several use non-MU moves (r/R/F-based) with alg.cubing.net links. Part 2 is long, unfinished draft notes on 1/1 cases. They are organised three different ways: by U/D layer placement; by L/R edge 'quality' (good/bad orientation), then relative position, then corners; and by relative position, then quality, then corners. Each branch gives a numbered step-by-step intuitive solution with move counts and probabilities (e.g. '7 or 9 moves, 1:3 probability'). Part 2 also defines 'DP = Default Position' (the two bad edges a U2 apart from being stacked) and starts a '2o/2 + 4/0' section that is never finished. Saved: text and HTML exports and the 10 images (eolr-eolrb-imgs/). Structure: Notation (star = EOLRb) > EO section with EO diagram > L/R position-pair entries with corner-relation (SAME/OPP/ADJ) sub-branches; then nested outline notes for 1/1 cases (three alternative hierarchies), a 'Default Position' definition and an unfinished 2o/2+4/0 outline.

resources.title: EOLRb (PiKeeper's EOLRb doc)
resources.author: PiKeeper (the preface says to contact them on the Roux Discord as @pikeeper)
resources.level: advanced: the preface says it assumes full EOLR is already learned
resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc (no images) with STM-optimal EOLRb solutions for every EOLR case, built on top of the 'EOLR' doc, which it links to. Preface: when the EOLRb solution is just 'normal EOLR with a cancelled move at the end', it refers to that EOLR doc's solution. Many cases have several solutions of equal length, so readers should check their own solution's move count. There is no consensus on whether every case is worth learning. Comments and Discord messages are welcome. Structure: the same 9 EO groups (3/1, 4/0, 2o/2, 2a/2, 1/1, 2o/0, 2a/0, 0/2, 4/2) and the same named L/R-placement cases as the EOLR doc. A few cases are split further, e.g. 3/1 'Bad' into Misoriented Opposite / Diag / Misoriented / Mixed Opposite / Other. Each named case splits into sub-cases by how the L/R edge colours relate to the L/R corner colours: 'Matching', 'Opposite', 'Adjacent' or combinations, and 'Front'/'Sides' for where the L/R corners are. Each sub-case gives a 2-gen alg, a 'Recognition:' line and 'Solution (N move optimal)' with STM counts from 1 to 13. The solution is one of three kinds: 'Normal EOLR', 'Normal EOLR with cancellation at the end', or a separate intuitive reduction to another case. One case is marked '*Please don't learn this, the recognition is atrocious'. Count: 58 named cases with about 104 leaf sub-cases. By group: 3/1 10 named/18 leaves, 4/0 4/6, 2o/2 6/11, 2a/2 7/12, 1/1 11/21, 2o/0 6/13, 2a/0 7/11, 0/2 4/8, 4/2 3/4. Saved: text and HTML exports. Structure: Preface > EO group (bad-edge code + positions) > named L/R-placement case > corner-relation sub-case (Matching/Opposite/Adjacent, Front/Sides) with alg > Recognition > 'Solution (N move optimal)' + solution type.

resources.title: DFDB Recognition method for pauseless 4c (linked as "Anto's DFDB")
resources.author: Anto (Anto Kam, author of rouxl.es, which links the same method as a DFDB flowchart image). The final 'opposite DFDB' section is credited to XtremeCubez, with a link to their YouTube channel.
resources.level: intermediate to advanced (LSE look-ahead: predicting the 4c case during 4b)
resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc that teaches DFDB recognition, so 4c (the final M-slice edges) can be predicted before 4b (ULUR insertion) is finished, removing the pause between them. It has 20 embedded 3D cube images (yellow top, white DF/DB edges) and 7 worked examples, each given as a setup alg. The method is a short decision tree. (1) Define the DFDB edges: the two edges that belong in DF/DB. Their colours depend on the block colours. (2) Cycle (3-edge) or 2e2e (4-edge) case: just before the ULUR insertion (M2, or the M' U2 M'-style insertions), look at the U face. DFDB edges opposite each other mean 2e2e, adjacent mean a cycle. Everything after this is about cycles only. (3) Matching or non-matching centre: does the DFDB edge in the M-slice match the front or back centre? The back has to be worked out from what is visible at the front. (4a) Matching: after the M2, AUF so the U-layer DFDB edge lines up with the centre of its colour, i.e. the DFDB edges end up opposite. Then solve the remaining DFDB edge intuitively with short M/U2 triggers, sometimes 3 moves. (4b) Non-matching: the AUF after the M2 has to solve the corners, and you track where the DFDB edges go. If they are stacked (one on top of the other, e.g. FU/FD), a fixed two-move sequence turns it into a matching case. If they are opposite (e.g. FU/BD), the XtremeCubez section gives a fixed 4-step procedure: M or M' to bring the non-matching edge up, U2, M or M' to bring the resulting 'line' up, then U2 M2. No alg table; 3 procedure branches (matching; non-matching stacked; non-matching opposite) after the cycle/2e2e split. Saved: text and HTML exports and the 20 images (anto-dfdb-imgs/). Structure: Concept (DFDB edges, cycle vs 2e2e) > cycle-only rules > matching vs non-matching centre > matching procedure with 2 worked examples > non-matching procedure (corner-solving AUF, position tracking) > stacked rule with 1 example > opposite rule (credited to XtremeCubez) with 2 examples.
